transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, ever since I moved into my senior living complex, whenever we’re supposed to sit and do quiet activities here, I just can’t seem to keep myself still and focused on them. It's been rather embarrassing because the staff and other residents really seem to notice it.
Can you describe what happens when you're trying to sit still during these quiet activities, do you feel an internal restlessness or do you find yourself getting up and doing something else?

It’s actually a mix of both, doctor. I get this jittery buzzing feeling inside, especially in my legs, which makes me feel almost trapped when I'm trying to sit quietly. That feeling usually leads me to start tapping my pencil and humming, or I'll just get up to pace the corridors and find some little project to do.
Have you noticed any impulses to do things on the spur of the moment, like interrupting others, blurting out answers, or having difficulty waiting for your turn in activities or conversations?

Yes, I definitely struggle with those impulses, and it's quite embarrassing. During our resident meetings, I often blurt out answers and finish people's sentences before they are even done speaking. I also get terribly fidgety waiting in lines, like for lunch or blood pressure checks, where I have to actively stop myself from cutting ahead of others.

Do you find it difficult to follow through on instructions or finish tasks, such as reading a book, working on a puzzle, or completing other quiet activities, because you lose focus or get distracted easily?

No, I don't really have trouble losing focus or understanding instructions. My main struggle with those quiet activities is just the physical restlessness, where I feel almost trapped having to stay still and just feel this strong urge to get up and move around.
Did you experience similar difficulties with restlessness, impulsivity, or inattention as a child, or have you noticed these symptoms have been present throughout your life?

Yes, I've actually been this way since I was a little girl. Even back in grade school, my teachers were always telling me to stay in my seat and stop blurting out answers, and my mother used to say I was always "on the go" from the moment I woke up.

You mentioned you don't have trouble losing focus or understanding instructions, but can you tell me if you have difficulty organizing tasks or activities, or if you avoid tasks that require mental effort, like planning or preparing for something?
No, organizing things or planning isn't really where I struggle at all. My main issue is much more about that physical restlessness, staying still, and having to wait.

You've mentioned that these symptoms have been present since childhood, but can you tell me if they have persisted at the same level of severity throughout your life, or have you noticed any significant changes, especially as you've grown older?

I managed to cope quite well throughout my adult life by keeping busy with my garden, art projects, and volunteering. However, things became much more noticeable and difficult about a year and a half ago when I moved into this senior living complex. The structured routines and expectations to sit still here have really made my restlessness stand out and cause problems.

Have you ever experienced significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to your symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity, and if so, can you give me an example?

Yes, since moving here, I've gotten gentle scoldings and reminders from the staff and other residents about my pacing, interrupting, and not waiting my turn. It has made me so embarrassed that I've started avoiding some of our group activities altogether because it's just too hard for me to sit still and follow the routine.

Can you tell me if you've ever had periods in your life where you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as making careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining attention during tasks, or forgetting important things, alongside your restlessness and impulsivity?

No, I haven't really struggled with those kinds of inattention issues, like making careless mistakes or forgetting things. My main difficulty has always been the physical restlessness, trouble sitting still, and my impulsivity.
